玩了这款后，渴望冷兵器近距离战斗那就玩mortal sin，想要热兵器射击就来玩这款voidborn！ 超级棒，作为肉鸽游戏，也有箱庭的探索趣味，在第二关之后，就不要局限于战斗区域了，利用主角的高性能可以到各个地方去看看，可以找到丰富的奖励！不过可一定要记得路，像是第三关我怎么找都找不到BOSS。。 第一人称肉鸽中少有的让我如此惊喜的游戏，打击感和手感太棒了，目前感觉唯一缺点可能就是祝福强化部分不够有趣，而且不知道是不是我的问题，有时射着射着就会自动卡壳，按老半天不会射击。 游戏世界观一股魂味，开局基地就是火鸡场吧，以我目前的游玩体验到的只有饰品（类似空洞骑士的纹章）与铁匠处的武器，希望后续更新能更丰富一点。 游戏难度还是蛮高的，部分敌人伤害也太夸张了，回血数值也低，希望制作组能调整一下。 希望正式版发售后能有中文！

So heavily inspired by ULTRAKILL it almost borders on theft. So far I've only made it to the second area, wouldn't usually write a review at this point but only one of the enemies I've encountered doesn't have some direct counterpart in ULTRAKILL. I would describe the general feel of this game as ULTRAKILL but worse. So far the roguelike elements don't really add much, the upgrades don't feel especially meaningful, and I barely notice a difference when I'm reset. The game is also plagued by a number of design issues, some so large they make me wonder whether the only good parts were taken directly from ULTRAKILL.

Many enemies get stuck, I glitched into the lava and took no damage once, gun animations are jittery as if they weren't finished (early access stuff I know) and once the game decided it didn't want to recognise my mouse movement mid game while my mouse buttons still worked that's the moment when I knew I was refunding the game Hopefully it only gets better from here because I love the aesthetic alot so maybe one day I'll return back to this game when its in a better state

Wasted potential. Just a copy paste of a few games put together of ULTRAKILL, Dark Souls and near any rogue like/lite First hour and a half was fun doing runs, leaning, etc. But the whole weapon rarity thing is a lie. It's purely dependant on what weapon has what attribute. (E.G Revolver with the void legendary, which is also mid as hell mind you). The game's bosses are actually near rip offs. Last boss is s Temu version of V2 from ULTRAKILL. Not to mention the twins boss fight is a straight rip from Dark Souls, plus the area of the boss was heavily inspired. Lack of weapons in the game is clear as day. From run TWO OR THREE you could have all FOUR weapons in the game. And it's not even close to mention the best one is the shotgun, followed by the base revolver. It's ridiculous that there was such potential to be used and it was wasted harshly. The AR is a joke in terms of dmg, and the sword is ok I suppose due to the parry... But even then, we already have a built in parry so there's genuinely 0 point to it. Not to mention bugs in the game. I'm aware this is a 1.0 from beta release and I understand there may be a few... But I seriously don't understand 1. The common occurrence of enemies re-spawning near endlessly, and 2. The shocking render distance mostly prominent in the second area. Again, I'm aware it is a base game release, but bugs like these in a game like this makes it even less enjoyable to experience. Took me 4 runs to beat the game. Let alone the twin bosses and the final boss were purely gank. As for the second boss(es), it's three unneccesarry phases which is already a bad start. First phase is one of the twins, then it's both of the twins with an joint healthbar which makes it a pushover. Finally thr third phase is as cliche as it could ever be. One twin dies, other gets super angry, cue new phase with incerdibly buffed abilities... The worst part is it's easily beaten by constantly sliding sideways and shooting. TL;DR, unnecessary cliche three phases, either cheese to win or die. Last boss is a mirror match, which I personally say doesn't add up to lore, and more or less thought was a second to final considering their speech. Though that's my personal opinion. Though what IS factual is the fact it's so unfathomably bland, doing the same exact three attacks. Which turned out to be a false nine for a stupid second phase which is practically first phase on two weeks dosage of heroin. Bigger sword so hitbox is bigger, stupid amount of hp, and the same attacks as first phase but with a little flair to 'spice it up'. Another thing to mention is the lack of scaling enemies. If I'm in the final area of the game I'm not expecting to see the most basic two enemies that still gets one shot. This is a roguelike/lite. It goes without saying the further you go, the harder you expect the enemies to be. Not to have them as useless fodder. There isn't variety in the game, this feels like more like a poor storytelling game that took other game's parts and tried making it fit, when in reality it made it 50 times worse. Would honestly just play a roguelike MOD for ULTRAKILL. Yes, I would rather play a mod for a game than this game itself, because ULTRAKILL is unique in its own way. people see it as original while I see this as a poor excuse for a game. This is, simply put, a bad, unnecessary mix of games that didn't need to happen nor do I want to ever see it. The original plan with the void stopping demi-gods is a great idea on paper and I'd even say I like it. But the excecution with it? Abysmal. Twin demigods? And since when was the 'fallen Voidborn' a demigod? It makes 0 sense lore wise or gameplay wise and it makes things worse because it leaves unanswered questions with no response. The game felt like it ended the minute it truly began. Putting four 'demi gods', two being near rip offs and the other two being actually unique in a sense feels like lazy design. I would've thought we would have been given a number to how many demi gods, and described what they were the god for, like the first one being of war... Though the idea very clearly god left behind seeing as the other 'demi gods' just have the title and nothing more. Overall? Unbalanced weapons, lack OF weapons, unbalanced difficulty in bosses (the third one is by far easiest for no reason), lack of upgrades and having them be capped at 5th level stupidly, poor overall bosses design, poor storytelling, and just lack of a game. I felt like I played a third of what I thought i would experience. The 'final boss' left the story near abruptly and with a cliche way. Big castle gets stormed, up top big final boss awaits. It's boring an uncreative. This is being made during the 1.0 release. And I honestly have 0 hope for the game in general. Secret areas are literally time wasters that give you LESS UPGRADES than the main path, making them the thing you look at and turn away without a second thought. I don't suggest this game whatsoever since for not much more money, you can easily get ULTRAKILL and mod it with a roguelike mod for a MUCH better experience than what this gives.

I really wish I could recommend this game, because a roguelike game with ultrakill style combat seemed right up my alley, but nothing about this game is fun to me, the movement feels really bad and the builds are so one dimensional.

The game is fun, it can run on a potato because it's made on, Unreal Engine 4 and has low poly visuals. It is not as aim-intensive as something like CS, but it still rewards clean aim, especially early on when you are using a pistol that can instantly kill most enemies if you flick to their heads. Pair that with Titanfall-style movement and constant projectile dodging, and the game really does capture that older, simpler arena-shooter feeling. Personally, Voidborn hits a very specific niche for me. It feels like a light aim-trainer wrapped inside an arcadey FPS campaign, except it is also a proper roguelike. It is not as chaotic or build-heavy as games like Gunfire Reborn or Roboquest, which lean much harder into looter-shooter variety, tons of weapons, and wild builds. Voidborn feels more grounded by comparison, and while that might make it more niche, I am honestly grateful that this game exists. There are other things like parry mechanics, grenade tosses, stomping AOE abilities, alot of good stuff from Ultrakill

I played this game in its demo and, while I thought it needed some work, it seemed like it could be a good game. I should preface by saying that this isn't a bad game, but I wouldn't go as far as to call it good either. Any build you can make gets pretty repetitive after one playthrough, and it makes each replay feel very samey. Every boss leading up to the final boss is, frankly, piss easy. So long as you have a semblance of an idea on how to make an effective build, you'll steamroll every boss save for the final boss. The final boss feels like it was made for a game with ULTRAKILL-like movement as opposed to the movement this game has. Movement is pretty sluggish and most of your mobility just comes in some variation of a dash. I really love the art direction when it comes to the environments, but I feel like the enemy and weapon design is often lacking. The upgrades you can get after each run seem inconsequential and frankly unnecessary. I've also noticed in a few areas that there seems to be clipping issues in certain parts of the map. Specifically, while in the sacred grove, I got clipped into a pillar. Anytime I would try to get out, I would instantly fall into acid and then be teleported back inside the pillar until I eventually died. Overall I'm pretty disappointed with how this game turned out. However, it could be a good game to play for an hour if you're bored.
